annotation.authors_or_issuer: Gonçalves, P.J.S.; Santos, S.; Lourenço, B.; Pereira, C.; Pinheira, V.; Moreira, M.J.G.; et al.
annotation.summary_en: Conference paper describing four cognitive games for nursing-home elders, the last using a tele-operated car-like robot, and discussing the ethical issues addressed in design and trials with 50 elders in two Portuguese nursing homes, including beneficence/non-maleficence, deception and infantilisation.
annotation.title_clean: From traditional games to robotic games: ethical issues with elders
annotation.title_en: From traditional games to robotic games: ethical issues with elders
annotation.venue: ICRES 2019: International Conference on Robot Ethics and Standards, London
key_provisions_or_claims: Four incrementally harder cognitive games adapted from nursing-home games; the fourth uses a tele-operated robot.
Ethical issues drawn from literature (Sharkey & Sharkey) and handled during design and trials.
Concerns include beneficence/do no harm, deception and infantilisation of elders.
Tested with 50 elders in two Portuguese nursing homes.
Authors conclude the system is ethically proper.
